plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on upright stems above broad, blue-green leaves. Thousands of cultivars exist, with single, double, fringed, and parrot-petaled forms. In temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens, early May is peak or late-peak tulip season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring (April to early May in temperate Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, North America, Europe, temperate Asia; native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: During the Dutch 'Tulip Mania' of the 1630s, single bulbs sold for more than the price of a house in Amsterdam.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub producing dense, conical clusters of intensely fragrant flowers. It thrives in cold-winter climates and is a classic feature of old gardens and homesteads. Peak bloom often falls in early to mid May across the northern United States, Canada, and northern Europe.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (late April to late May)
plants.location: Northern Europe, northern United States, Canada; native to the Balkan Peninsula
plants.funFact: Lilac is the official state flower of New Hampshire, and its fragrance is so beloved that perfumers often recreate it synthetically because the real flowers yield little essential oil.

plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: A vigorous woody twining vine that produces long, cascading racemes of pea-like, fragrant flowers. Japanese wisteria blooms open progressively from the base of each raceme to the tip. Famous wisteria tunnels in Japan reach peak display from late April into mid May.
plants.location: Japan (Ashikaga Flower Park, Kawachi Fuji Gardens), also cultivated in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Some wisteria vines live for over a century, and the Ushijima wisteria in Japan is estimated to be around 1,200 years old.

plants.name: Sophora japonica
plants.commonName: Chilean Wine Palm Alternative: Kōwhai (Sophora microphylla)
plants.description: Kōwhai is a small New Zealand native tree with drooping clusters of golden, tubular flowers that attract native birds such as tūī and bellbirds. Its flowering season in New Zealand runs from late winter to spring, though in some regions flowers may linger into early autumn on selected forms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in New Zealand (some forms bloom into autumn)
plants.funFact: The word 'kōwhai' is the Māori word for yellow, and traditionally the blooming of kōwhai signaled the time to plant kūmara (sweet potato).
